The instant petition has been filed praying for a writ of mandamus commanding the respondents to pay compensation to the petitioners in respect of Khasra No. 430(ka) area 0.1500 hectares of the revenue village Sudan Pur-A, Pargana, Tehsil and District Bareilly.

sentences.text:
The facts of the case have been noted in a previous order dated 09.01.2005 which is reproduced below:
"1.
It is not in dispute that the State respondents have utilized the land of the petitioners for construction of dam without any formal acquisition and payment of compensation in the year 2015-16.
On 16/17.02.2018, a Committee headed by the Collector, Bareilly decided to pay compensation to the affected persons at four times the circle rate.
The decision of the Committee was approved by the Commissioner on 06.04.2018.
The total amount assessed as compensation to be payable to the land owners was Rs. 4738.07 Lakhs.
The Commissioner directed the District Magistrate to take action in the matter accordingly.

However, till date the compensation has not been paid to the petitioner and they have been made to run from pillar to post,
compelling them to file the instant petition.
2. Learned Standing Counsel has placed on record the instructions received from Executive Engineer, Flood Division, Barelilly dated 26.08.2024.
Therein, it is not disputed that on 06.04.2018, the Commissioner, Bareilly Division approved the payment of compensation at four times the circle rate (Rs. 30,00,000/- per hectares).
The case taken is that thereafter relevant records were got prepared and on 14.08.2024, request has been sent to the Higher Officials for approval of the requisite funds.
It is stated that as soon as the funds are received a sale deed would be obtained from the petitioners and they would be paid compensation.
3. It is not disputed that the petitioners were deprived of possession of their land in the year 2015-16.
The compensation amount was approved by the Commissioner way back in the year, 2018.
It is wholly inexplicable as to why compensation has not been paid to the petitioners so far.
4. Sri Rajiv Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel for the State submits that as soon as the requisite funds are allocated for payment of compensation the same would be paid.
5. We do not approve the manner in which the State is proceeding in the instant case.
The land having been taken over in the year 2015-16 and compensation amount quantified in 2018, there was no justification for not paying the compensation.

We require the first respondents to ensure allocation of requisite funds and payment of compensation to the petitioners positively within three weeks alongwith interest from the date of dispossession, failing which respondent no.1 will file his personal affidavit and explain why this Court should not proceed to fix responsibility of the officers for delay in making the payment.
6. List this matter on 06.02.2025.

sentences.text: 7. Sri Rajiv Gupta, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel will communicate the instant order to the respondent no.1 for immediate compliance."

3. An affidavit has been filed by respondent no.4 disclosing that each petitioner is entitled to Rs.
42,000/- as compensation and 5% interest over it from 2015-16 and thus the total sum payable to each petitioner is Rs. 60,900/-.

It is also stated that notices were sent to the petitioners in January and February 2025 to approach him and complete certain formalities so that the compensation amount along with interest is paid to them.

4. Sri Suresh Singh, learned Additional Chief Standing Counsel submits that as soon as the petitioners complete all the formalities the compensation amount along with interest shall be released in their favour.
5. Counsel for the petitioners submits that amount quantified as compensation is acceptable to the petitioners.
However, the petitioners are entitled to interest from the year 2015-16 since when they were deprived of the possession of their properties.
6. It is not disputed even to the respondents that the interest would be payable from financial year 2015-16.
7. The interest has been calculated at the rate of 5% per annum, which is not acceptable to the petitioners.
They claim interest in terms of the provisions of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 and the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 8. Under both the aforesaid Acts, for the first year since date of dispossession, interest is payable at the rate of 9% per annum and subsequent year at the rate of 15% per annum.
9. In our considered opinion, the petitioners are also entitled to interest as per the provisions of the aforesaid two enactments.

The respondents cannot be permitted to flout the provisions of law by initially taking possession of land of private persons without initiating proceedings for acquisition under the relevant legislation and thereafter also not paying interest at the rate provided under law.
10.

Accordingly, we dispose of the instant petition with direction to the State respondents to ensure payment of interest at the rate of 9% per annum for the first year since date of dispossession and 15% for the subsequent period till date of actual payment along with the compensation as has been already approved provided the petitioners complete all the formalities as may be required of them.
11. In respect of Khasra No. 192(ka) which according to the respondents, has not been utilized, it shall be open to the petitioners to apply for demarcation.
(Anish Kumar Gupta, J.) (Manoj Kumar Gupta, J.) Order Date :- 6.2.2025

Ashish Pd.
